messages:
morgan: Heads-up — we started seeing a recurring 503 pattern from hosted inference for a single large customer over the past 2 hours. It's specific to streaming generate calls (http2) and correlates with lots of small concurrent streams (20-80 per client).

sam: Any traceback or logs yet? customer on SDK or raw HTTP?

morgan: Customer uses our python SDK with multiplexing enabled. Repro I've run locally: open 50 streaming connections that send short prompts repeatedly. ~30-40% of streams hit 503 within ~30s. No obvious model OOMs.

morgan: Minimal repro script (python, uses our sdk stream):
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
streams = []
for i in range(50):
    streams.append(c.generate_stream(prompt="short prompt", model="open-instruct-v1"))
# read simultaneously
for s in streams:
    for chunk in s:
        pass
```

katie: Can you paste a snippet of the gateway logs around a 503?

morgan: Logs (edge/gateway) - redacted IDs:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] conn=xyz stream_id=17 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=120
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] conn=xyz stream_id=19 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=503 code=H2_WINDOW_STARVATION duration_ms=45
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] conn=xyz stream_id=21 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=503 code=H2_WINDOW_STARVATION duration_ms=50
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] conn=xyz stream_id=23 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=110
```

sam: H2_WINDOW_STARVATION looks familiar — indicates the server couldn't schedule data frames due to per-connection window exhaustion. Multiplexed clients can exhaust window quickly if many active streams.

miguel: Agreed. We saw a similar spike last year but tied to a buggy client that didn't respect DATA/WINDOW_UPDATE pacing. Two quick questions: 1) is this across regions? 2) does disabling multiplexing on the SDK reduce rate?

morgan: Customer ran a quick test: disabling HTTP/2 multiplexing (force single stream per connection) dropped 503s to <1%. So looks client multiplexing -> window exhaustion on our edge. Region: only US-WEST for this customer currently.

eng-runtime: @morgan thanks for the repro. Possible mitigations: 1) increase per-connection initial window/flow-control on edge proxy (risk larger memory usage), 2) enforce per-connection concurrent stream limits, 3) add adaptive WINDOW_UPDATE pacing on server side to prioritize fairness.

katie: For short-term customer impact, can we suggest an interim workaround?

sam: Workaround for customer: (a) disable client multiplexing in SDK (b) use connection pooling with fewer concurrent streams per connection (set max_conns higher, streams_per_conn lower) (c) add client-side small backoff between stream opens. 

morgan: I drafted a customer note to send once we confirm steps. Please review: 

"Support note (draft): Hi — we've identified a pattern where high counts of concurrent streaming requests over a single HTTP/2 connection can cause gateway-level window starvation and lead to intermittent 503 responses. Short-term workaround: disable HTTP/2 multiplexing in the SDK or reduce streams-per-connection. We're implementing edge-side mitigations and will follow up with a permanent fix and timeline. Sorry for the disruption — we'll update you in 3 hours with progress.

If you'd like, we can schedule a debug session to run the repro with your app while monitoring logs."

miguel: Looks good. Add that we recommend SDK v0.9.4+ which has a flag to toggle multiplexing.

eng-runtime: For the engineering action items:
- Increase per-conn window by +50% on a small canary subset (us-west-host-7) and watch memory and 503 rate.
- Instrument WINDOW_UPDATE metrics and per-stream queue lengths.
- Add a circuit-breaker to temporarily reject new streams on a conn after N consecutive H2_WINDOW_STARVATION events.

sam: I'll run the canary change now and post results.

incident-bot: Deploy started: edge-config/us-west-host-7 window-increase -> rollout 1/1

morgan: Thanks — looping in @support-bot to keep customer updated once we have data.

support-bot: Draft message queued to customer chat. ETA next update 60-90m.

sam: Canary results after 12m: host shows 503 rate for this flow dropped from 38% -> 4%. Memory usage bump +6% on host, stream queue depth reduced. No new error modes observed.

eng-runtime: Promising. Let's hold 30m then roll to 3 more hosts. Also start task to implement server-side adaptive window pacing as medium-term fix.

katie: Customer comms ready — send now?

morgan: Send now and mention the temporary mitigation and recommended SDK switch. I'll include repro artifacts and logs. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Sent to customer at 2026-03-17T14:45Z.

morgan: Closing loop — will file an engineering ticket for adaptive pacing and per-conn stream circuit-breaker, link after created. Great quick team response. :clap:
